subject.title: Feature request: native Codex quota/auth diagnosis plus brokered reauth execution

question: Should OpenClaw add a native Codex provider recovery-state contract, and should any brokered reauth execution remain explicit/operator-controlled or be allowed to start from diagnosis automatically?
rationale: The remaining work requires maintainer intent because it defines provider/Gateway/UI API shape and a security-sensitive OAuth host-execution boundary.

options.title: Typed status first
options.body: Define `quota_wait` versus `reauth_required` across provider status, Gateway, and UI while leaving reauth execution explicit through current bounded login flows.

options.title: Adopt `/login codex` as enough
options.body: Close the brokered execution part as covered by explicit private-channel/Web UI pairing and only polish status/copy around it.

options.title: Permit auto brokered reauth
options.body: Allow diagnosis-triggered broker execution, accepting the need for a dedicated security review, authorization model, expiry, audit, and anti-spam controls.

recommendation.title: Typed status first
recommendation.body: Define `quota_wait` versus `reauth_required` across provider status, Gateway, and UI while leaving reauth execution explicit through current bounded login flows.

likelyOwner.reason: Their current-main Codex quota/status work is closest to the typed recovery-state part of the remaining decision.
